info.title: Tollkit
info.description: Pay-per-call tools for AI agents: web pages, PDFs and search; SEC filings, weather, airport delays, geocoding, IP and exchange rates; wallets and tokens on Base, Ethereum and Solana; product prices; signed page proofs. No account, no API key: pay in-band with x402 in USDC on Base or Solana. Each operation's server is its product line's hostname. Other Tollkit tools are described at: https://attest.tollkit.dev/openapi.json, https://web.tollkit.dev/openapi.json, https://chain.tollkit.dev/openapi.json, https://data.tollkit.dev/openapi.json.
info.x-guidance: Give POST /extract the URL of ONE product page and it returns schema.org/Product JSON — name, brand, sku, price, currency, availability, images, variants. The page is rendered in a real headless browser and the store's own schema.org data is read before anything is inferred, so JavaScript-built pages work and sku/variants come from the source. Every response carries a `provenance` object saying which fields the merchant declared and which the model inferred, so you can tell a published price from a read one. Use POST /extract/batch when you have more than one URL: up to 5 for one flat payment and one round trip, which is the usual case when comparing a product across stores. GET /preview is free and returns a real extraction of a fixed sample page, so you can judge output quality before spending anything. Failed extractions are never charged. A URL that redirects to what looks like a different page is refused free rather than answered with the wrong product; pass allow_redirect to override. Cached answers say so and carry the original render timestamp.

post.summary: Extract structured Product data from one product page URL
post.description: Product details from one product page URL: price, currency, stock, name, brand, SKU/GTIN, images and variants as schema.org/Product JSON, with which fields the store itself published. $0.01 per call; a page it cannot read is not charged.

url.description: Absolute https:// URL of ONE product page. Not a search or category page, not a login-gated page, and not a private address.

allow_redirect.description: By default a URL that redirects to what looks like a different page (a discontinued item bouncing to its category listing) is refused free of charge rather than answered with the wrong product.

schema.description: schema.org/Product extracted from the rendered page. Fields the page does not state come back null rather than guessed.

currency.description: ISO 4217. Null whenever price is null.

images.description: Up to 5 absolute URLs copied from the page. Never invented.

fetchedAt.description: ISO timestamp of the RENDER, not of this call. Older than now on a cached result.

cached.description: True when re-served from a recent render. Still a paid call, and the data is as old as cache_age_seconds says.

provenance.description: Where each field came from. `declared` fields match what the merchant published in schema.org JSON-LD or Open Graph tags — their own number, the one they stand behind. `inferred` fields were read off the page by a model and deserve less trust. Fields that came back null appear in neither list. Use this to decide which values you can act on directly and which are worth a second look.
